author: Autodesk
description: This graph demonstrates a liquid sim informed and guided by a spectral ocean.
documentation:
## Guided Liquid Simulation

### What it does

This graph creates a liquid simulation that is guided and informed by a spectral simulation.

### Inputs and outputs

This graph is self-contained and generates inputs.

### How it works

- A guided liquid simulation is defined inside a region of space called a simulation region, and is one-way coupled to a guide surface which can originate from spectral and dynamic waves, or even a lower resolution liquid simulation.

- The guided simulation inherits the overall motion from the guide, but facilitates simulating the full 3D motion of the liquid inside the simulation region at higher resolution to capture interaction with colliders as well as breaking waves and foam.

- Liquid particles that exit the simulation region can collide and be dragged along with the guide surface until they are eventually erased based on age. A secondary wave ripple solve can be added to more faithfully capture the interaction of the escaped particles with the guide surface.

_notes.text:
# ***guided_liquid_simulation***

A guided liquid simulation is defined inside a region of space called a simulation region, and is one-way coupled to a guide surface which can originate from spectral and dynamic waves, or even a lower resolution liquid simulation.

The guided simulation inherits the overall motion from the guide, but facilitates simulating the full 3D motion of the liquid inside the simulation region at higher resolution to capture interaction with colliders as well as breaking waves and foam.

Liquid particles that exit the simulation region can collide and be dragged along with the guide surface until they are eventually erased based on age. A secondary wave ripple solve can be added to more faithfully capture the interaction of the escaped particles with the guide surface.
The ***simulation_region*** controls the area in which the FLIP simulation will be calculated.  The ***diagnostic*** flag will show the simulation region.

### ***foam_simulation***

The ***foam_simulation*** compound is an entire second simulation on top of the guided liquid that generates foam particles.

Due to its processing overheads, its display (and therefore generation)  is switched ***off*** by default in this graph.

Feel free to switch it on in the ***render_and_display*** compound.

To avoid visual seams upon render, 
```
declare enable_physical_TIR constant BOOL enable_physical_TIR on
```

must be added in the Arnold render settings user options under Render settings -> Diagnostics -> User Options -> Options

If rendering using an ***aiSkyDomeLight***, set *camera* and *transmission* attributes to zero to avoid light transmission through the ocean from beneath.
As age-limit we use the same value as the age on the guided liquid outside the simulation region.
Masked emission tapers off emission near edges of simulation region.
Create a shell volume collider of ocean surface with hole in the middle.

_backdrops.title: Setup Alpha field for Masked Emission of Foam
Setup Ocean Surface Collider for the Foam

_notes.text: When caching to disk, compute the guide volume separately, since it's not being output from the solver (when using the liquid cache).

_backdrops.title: Guiding Influence To Dampen Velocities Near Edges of Guided Simulation
Cache Properties Required for Rendering and Foam Simulation

_notes.text:
#### **This compound controls the overall resolution of the guided simulation.  These settings will apply to the entire setup.**

***out_detail_size***:  This is the detail_size of the simulation, determined from *high_resolution*, *high_res_detail_size* and *low_res_detail_size*.

***out_volume_resolution_factor***: This is used by *points_to_liquid_surface* to divide *out_detail_size* to construct the detail size of the initial volume in the meshing stage from the liquid particles. It is determined from *volume_resolution_factor* on resolution_settings. This means that a larger resolution factor means lower detail.

***out_meshing_detail_size_scale*** is a resolution multiplier on the detail size of the volume from *out_volume_resolution_factor* for the mesh produced from the meshing. It's determined from *mesh_resolution_factor* on resolution_settings where again a number larger than 1 means higher resolution.

***ocean_mesh_detail_size*** is the detail size of the ocean mesh for rendering, ensuring it has the same resolution as the mesh produced from the meshing of the liquid particles.

### ***mesh_and_blend***

This compound converts liquid points to a mesh and blends with a guide volume near and outside the simulation regions.

There are **two main approaches to blending** simulated liquids with an ocean surface:

**Multi-pass rendering**:
The simulation and ocean are rendered separately and blended later using alpha compositing for maximum control.

Users are responsible for creating their own render setups and compositing workflow

**In-camera blending**:
Everything is rendered together in a single pass.

Visual artifacts such as seams, clipping, or blend imperfections may appear, particularly at lower simulation resolutions or in areas with heavy motion or splashing.
In this setup, a point size of .005 works well for high resolution.
